thread:
alex_support: Customer reported recurring SSE disconnects from our hosted API when using their mobile SDK (iOS v1.2.3). Symptoms: stream opens, a few events arrive (partial chunks possible), then after ~30-90s the connection is closed from server side. They see a 200 then abrupt socket close and get an auth error on next reconnect. Logs attached below.

aria_support: Thanks Alex. Any chance this lines up with token refreshes? customer said they refresh tokens proactively.

alex_support: They said token refresh happens at t+60s in our flows. Customer logs: 
```
[2024-05-14T18:12:03Z] SSE open: 200 OK, headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Content-Type: text/event-stream
[2024-05-14T18:12:35Z] RECEIVED: event chunk (partial)
[2024-05-14T18:13:03Z] write error: EPIPE (syscall write) -> socket closed by peer
[2024-05-14T18:13:03Z] reconnect attempt -> 401 unauthorized
```
They also included this server-side error from their capture: `write: connection reset by peer` and `SSE abort: backpressure limit exceeded`.

sam_oncall: Huh. We had a change in rate limiting/backpressure thresholds last month — but that should just queue not abort. @michael_runtime can you check whether token refresh midpoint could trigger our auth middleware to close the connection?

michael_runtime: Looking. Our auth path shouldn't actively close 200 streams on token rotation. But the backpressure aborts are triggered by socket write blocking for >500ms then a hard abort in runtime to avoid resource leakage. That code path was introduced for connection storms last quarter.

customer_relay: To reproduce on our side we use a mobile client that buffers reads slowly. Repro steps we gave: 
1) open SSE with SDK, keep client read loop intentionally sleeping 200ms between reads
2) cause token refresh at t+60s (OAuth refresh)
3) observe partial chunk + connection close.

aria_support: Can you paste a minimal repro curl/node example we can run?

customer_relay: Yeah, here's a Node repro we used (simplified):
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=test', {
    headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <short-lived>' }
  });
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  while(true){
    const {value, done} = await reader.read();
    if(done) break;
    // simulate slow consumer
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, 180));
    console.log('chunk', value && value.length);
  }
})();
```

alex_support: When they add `socket.setNoDelay(true)` in their SDK the disconnects appear less frequent but not gone. They also saw fewer disconnects when they extended refresh to >120s.

sam_oncall: That points to interplay between token refresh (brief spike of extra control traffic), slow drain on send buffer and our backpressure safety abort. Two hypotheses: (1) token refresh causes short additional write (auth ping) that pushes socket write over threshold; (2) auth middleware momentarily rewrites headers causing connection renegotation.

michael_runtime: I pulled logs for the customer session id from our ingress cluster around that time: we see repeated EAGAIN on write to socket, then our connection abort path with message `backpressure window exceeded: 512kb` at 18:13:03. No 401s from our side prior to abort. After abort the client tries reconnect and the token refresh sequence results in 401 because refresh wasn't completed yet. So flow is: slow consumer -> write stall -> runtime aborts -> client reconnects with stale token -> 401.

aria_support: Good find. So fix paths: suggest immediate mitigations for customer + long-term engineering changes.

alex_support: Recommended immediate mitigations provided to customer: 
- Increase client read frequency or reduce simulated sleep (from 180ms to <=50ms).
- Use `socket.setNoDelay(true)` to reduce buffering latency.
- If possible, stagger token refresh (renew on background connection) so refresh does not coincide with heavy write bursts.

customer_relay: Tried reducing sleep to 50ms and added setNoDelay: disconnects dropped from ~40% to ~6% in our test. Good.

sam_oncall: For long term, we should: 
- Add a softer backpressure strategy: gradual throttling / 429 to producers instead of hard abort.
- Track per-connection token-refresh events in runtime to avoid simultaneous write spikes.
- Increase default backpressure window on mobile tier.

michael_runtime: I'll open a runtime issue: RUNTIME-3124 (soft backpressure mode + token-refresh awareness). For immediate safety we can increase the abort threshold for hosted-tier by +2x, but that will increase memory/sockets in worst-case. Ops: any objections?

ops-bot: Incident policy check: changing host-wide thresholds requires a canary and ops approval. Please file OPS-REQ if proceeding.

alex_support: Filed OPS-REQ-6791 referencing RUNTIME-3124 and included customer repro. Also asked customer to share PCAP if they can.

aria_support: Can someone from devex draft a small best-practices note for mobile SDKs (setNoDelay, read loop, token refresh timing)? I'll add to support KB. @michael_runtime can you include recommended default thresholds?

michael_runtime: Will add recommendations to the ticket. For now I suggest documentation snippet: 
- Ensure read loop drains at least every 100ms on mobile networks.
- Use TCP_NODELAY for streaming sockets.
- Avoid refreshing auth tokens during active streaming sessions; prefer background refresh + swap on reconnect.

customer_relay: Thanks everyone — applying changes and will report back. I can share PCAP once we do a controlled test.

sam_oncall: Great. Marking this thread for escalation to eng-runtime and devex. I'll follow up in the bug RUNTIME-3124. :thumbsup:
